chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-A'ala ibn al-Fudayl and Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Look at your heart, so when it rejects your companion, then one of you has done something wrong (innovated/changed).'

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: Has done something new/innovated (introduced a fault or change)
key_terms.قَلْبُ: Heart (spiritual center of perception and emotion)

ai.seo_question: How do I know if I have a spiritual fault in my relationship with a companion?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the heart as a spiritual barometer for the health of social bonds, advising believers to observe internal aversion as a sign that one party has introduced a fault (*muhdith*). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *mu'asharah* (companionship) and the dynamic nature of spiritual states, where inner discord often precedes outward conflict. The advice underscores the importance of self-reflection (*muhasabah*) to identify whether the change stems from oneself or the companion, preserving the sanctity of the relationship.
